newsitem.title: FRANCE: Peugeot may cut back to one China plant.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot may cut back to one China plant.

text.p: Peugeot Automobiles, a division of the PSA Peugeot Citroen group, is studying the possibility of concentrating its production in China in one plant from two currently, a Peugeot spokesman said on Thursday.

"We're having some difficulties -- all western carmakers are having difficulties in China," the spokesman told Reuters. "We're studying whether we should maintain two sites or one," he said, but added that no decision had been made.
The Figaro newspaper reported on Wednesday that Peugeot may pull out of Guangzhou, citing pressure from Chinese authorities reported in the China Daily.
Peugeot produces 505 and 504 models in the southern city of Guangzhou, while the group's Citroen division produces ZX models in another, more modern plant in the central city of Wuhan.

The Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile Co, which is 30 percent owned by Peugeot, has produced only 100,000 cars since it went into production in 1986. The Peugeot spokesman said the carmaker was experiencing difficulties both in the production and sales.
But, he added, "We have every intention to stay in China."
Although China is viewed as a huge opportunity for carmakers seeking new markets, there is little payoff at the moment as it has one of the lowest vehicle density rates in the world.

The Figaro said Peugeot had been criticised by Chinese authorities for producing dated models. It said one of the possibilities Peugeot was considering was setting up the assembly of its new 406 sedans at the Wuhan plant.
